slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content: Vertical Tasting — Reading Aging Potential — This course covers Savennières, Chinon, and Vouvray, exploring how Loire's key red and white wines evolve across vintages and how to read aging potential from structure, acidity, and terroir.
slides.1.title: Vertical Tasting — Reading Aging Potential
slides.1.content:
This course systematically explores the terroir characteristics of Savennières, Chinon, and Vouvray, with a focus on vertical tasting methodology. Understanding how Chenin Blanc (Savennières/Vouvray) and Cabernet Franc (Chinon) develop across 5-, 10-, and 20-year windows is the key to unlocking Loire's true value proposition.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics during tasting.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following AOCs is the primary focus of this course?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Savennières is a key Loire AOC studied in this course alongside Chinon and Vouvray. Located on the north bank of the Loire in Anjou, it produces 100% Chenin Blanc dry white wines from volcanic schist soils. Its famously austere, high-acid young wines can age 10–30 years, evolving from mineral and citrus notes into complex layers of beeswax, dried apricot, and toasted hazelnut.
